title: Pop-up Book Paper Craft Animation

promptText: Pop-up book paper craft animation, 15 seconds, 16:9. Masterpiece paper engineering. Multi-layered topographic paper design, intricate cut-paper landscapes, embossed details, gold foil map markings, moving paper mechanisms, handcrafted textures, cinematic warm lighting, shallow depth of field. Everything exists as physical paper emerging from an antique atlas. No voice. Audio: turning pages, rustling paper, subtle orchestral wonder. ACT 1 (0-4s) An ancient atlas opens. A magnificent paper map unfolds across both pages. Mountains rise in layered paper relief. Forests, rivers, bridges, cities, and ships emerge from hidden folds. Tiny paper clouds float above the landscape. Camera travels low across the terrain. ACT 2 (4-8s) A page turns. The map begins reorganizing itself. Rivers fold upward into roads. Mountains flatten and transform into oceans. Cities slide across hidden paper tracks. Entire regions rotate and lock into new positions like a giant mechanical puzzle. ACT 3 (8-12s) Another page turns. The map becomes increasingly impossible. New continents unfold from beneath existing continents. Bridges span across the sky. Floating islands emerge from layered mechanisms. Endless paper geography grows outward beyond the original map. ACT 4 (12-15s) Final page turn. The entire world folds inward through thousands of synchronized paper movements, transforming into a giant ornate compass made from landscapes, cities, oceans, and mountains. The compass expands and unfolds into an even larger impossible map extending beyond the book's edges. Freeze on the completed transformation.

title: High-Speed Motorcycle Action Sequence
description: A dynamic action prompt for a motorcycle chase or racing scene with heavy speed blur and multiple cinematic cuts.
promptText:
Create an explosive, high-speed motorcycle action sequence in 16:9, 24fps, exactly 16 distinct cuts, total runtime ≈ 16–17 seconds.

A lone rider in a light green helmet and dark riding gear pilots a babypink sportbike along a narrow, winding paved mountain road that cuts through rolling green hills under a brilliant sunny sky with scattered white clouds and distant blue mountain ranges and water visible on the horizon. Preserve the exact bike color, rider silhouette, road markings, green landscape, fencing and lighting throughout — never redesign them.

This film is 90 % pure kinetic camera motion and 10 % environmental beauty: aggressive low-to-high tracking shots, continuous forward motion with heavy speed blur, whip pans, snap zooms, sun flares and impact shakes. No text, no graphics, no logos — pure cinematic speed.

### CUT LIST

CUT 01 | 0.00–1.00s
Dynamic low-side tracking shot: red motorcycle accelerates away from a small parking area onto the winding asphalt road; lush green grass and fence posts streak past with heavy motion blur; bright sun flares at the top of the frame.

**CUT 02 | 1.00–2.00s**  
Camera rises and locks behind the rider as the bike climbs the first gentle incline; green hills roll on both sides, a lone tree appears ahead, distant mountains and water visible on the right.

**CUT 03 | 2.00–3.00s**  
Tight rear tracking; rider leans into a smooth left curve; the road surface and white dashed lines blur heavily; sun remains high and intense.

**CUT 04 | 3.00–4.00s**  
Bike powers up a steeper section of road; camera stays low and centered, grass and fence posts racing past on both sides; distant valley opens on the right.

**CUT 05 | 4.00–5.00s**  
High-speed straight section; camera drops even lower, almost road-level, capturing the red bike centered against the climbing green hillside and bright blue sky.

**CUT 06 | 5.00–6.00s**  
Rider continues the climb; camera rises slightly and banks with the road; lush green slopes fill the left and right frame edges with strong motion blur.

**CUT 07 | 6.00–7.00s**  
Bike approaches a crest; camera pulls back a fraction to reveal more of the endless green hills and the road stretching ahead under the bright sun.

**CUT 08 | 7.00–8.00s**  
Rider leans into the next curve; camera swings wide then snaps back, capturing the red bike against the steep green embankment and metal guardrail.

**CUT 09 | 8.00–9.00s**  
Tight following shot as the motorcycle accelerates past the guardrail; heavy speed blur on the grass and road surface; sun flare intensifies.

**CUT 10 | 9.00–10.00s**  
Camera tilts upward dramatically, almost looking straight up the road; the red bike becomes smaller against the vast blue sky and white clouds while still racing forward.

**CUT 11 | 10.00–11.00s**  
Sweeping aerial-style arc as the bike enters a wide left-hand hairpin; camera orbits slightly, revealing the full curve of the road, green slopes and distant mountains.

**CUT 12 | 11.00–12.00s**  
High-angle tracking shot looking down on the red motorcycle as it carves the long sweeping curve; the road and guardrail form a perfect arc against the green hillside.

**CUT 13 | 12.00–13.00s**  
Camera pulls higher still, showing the bike as a small red shape on the winding road that snakes across the vast green landscape toward distant valleys and peaks.

**CUT 14 | 13.00–14.00s**  
Rider continues through the open hillside section; camera descends slightly and tracks from a higher three-quarter rear angle, capturing the bike, road and rolling green terrain.

**CUT 15 | 14.00–15.00s**  
Wide high-angle shot of the motorcycle navigating the next gentle S-curve; a second distant vehicle appears briefly on the road ahead; lush green fields and scattered trees fill the frame.

**CUT 16 | 15.00–16.65s 
Final high-speed tracking shot as the red bike continues along the open mountain road; camera gradually rises and the frame fills with bright green hills, blue sky and soft sun flare; the sequence ends on a sense of endless forward motion.

### Editing & Sound  
Extremely aggressive rhythm — continuous forward tracking with occasional whip pans, snap zooms and speed ramps, heavy motion blur on every surface, strong sun flares and subtle impact shakes on every crest or curve. No text, no graphics, no slow-motion.  

BGM / Audio: electronic / indie-pop beat with driving drums, bright synths and rising energy that matches the speed of the bike. Engine roar, wind whooshes and tire sound on asphalt are locked to the picture as rhythmic elements. Peak energy in the middle curves and end with a bright, open sonic release.

Premium AAA quality, photorealistic cinematic rendering, pure speed and freedom aesthetic, consistent red sportbike and rider design, exactly 16 cuts.

title: Indian Village Zombie Chase Intercut
description: A sophisticated intercut sequence contrasting a mother-daughter relationship in a cold zombie reality versus a warm nostalgic memory, using professional cinema camera settings.
promptText: Create a 26-second ultra-cinematic intercut chase sequence set in an Indian village, built around two parallel versions of the same mother-daughter relationship. The film language must feel sophisticated, emotional, and visually precise — not like generic zombie content. This should feel like a serious, beautifully directed short sequence shot with an ARRI Alexa / Alexa Mini LF style image, cinematic dynamic range, rich texture, strong highlight rolloff, shallow depth when needed, and confident visual grammar. Use expressive but controlled camera movement: handheld urgency in the present, smoother lyrical movement in the memory world, elegant match cuts, motivated pans, lens breathing, and emotionally meaningful intercutting. Keep it grounded, human, and heartbreaking. The setting is a rural Indian village and adjoining fields — narrow mud paths, small homes, low boundary walls, patches of crops, wet earth, scattered trees, open field edges, and a recognizable village texture. The sequence has two visual worlds: 1. Present / Zombie Reality Cold, blue-grey, wet, lightly rainy, fearful. This is the real world. The mother is running in panic, crying and exhausted, being chased by her own zombified daughter. This world should have a subtle cool blue tinge, overcast sky, light rain, mud, breath, desperation, and danger. Camera movement here should feel tense and close — handheld but controlled, with occasional tracking alongside or behind. Rain should visibly strike skin, fabric, and leaves. The daughter is still recognizable as a child, but unsettling: pale skin tone, lifeless focus, feral movement, subtle veins, predatory urgency, wet hair clinging to her face. No exaggerated monster design. Keep her scary because she is still a little girl. 2. Memory / Dream World Warm, sunlit, nostalgic, soft, and emotionally idealized. This is not reality — it is the mother’s memory or dream overlay. Same geography, same movement patterns, but now it is a golden, dreamy late-afternoon memory with soft warm sunlight, gentle bloom, slightly diffused highlights, and a touch of dreamy lens softness. In this version, the little girl is alive, healthy, playable, and joyfully running after her mother. The mother is laughing and looking back with love. The emotional contrast is the entire point. Camera / Lens Grammar Use 35mm / 40mm / 50mm cinematic language for emotional medium tracking shots, occasional longer-lens compression for the chase, and one or two slightly wider lenses for geography. The intercutting should rely on motion matches: same turn, same gesture, same direction of movement, but different reality. Whenever possible, cut on action so the audience feels the memory and horror colliding. The present should feel sharper, wetter, more immediate. The memory should feel slightly dream-filtered and warmer, but still photoreal. Beat Structure 0:00–0:12 — Intercut Chase Open immediately in the cold world: the mother is already running through the village in panic, breathless, crying, slipping slightly on wet earth, looking back over her shoulder. Behind her, the zombie daughter is chasing her with disturbing speed. Rain falls lightly. We stay close and urgent. Start intercutting almost immediately with the warm memory version: in the same path or nearby field edge, the little girl playfully runs after her mother, laughing. The mother turns back in sunshine, smiling with that instinctive playful fear mothers do when pretending to be chased. The key is that the movement and blocking should rhyme. A turn in the present becomes a turn in the past. A backward glance in terror becomes a backward glance in laughter. A muddy footstep becomes a barefoot or dry footstep in sunlit dust or grass. A panicked reach becomes a playful reach. The cuts should become emotionally richer as the first 12 seconds progress. The audience must understand that the mother is not just being chased — she is also remembering what this child once was. 0:12–0:24 — Catch / Field / Play Intercut In the present, the mother stumbles and falls into a field or grassy patch at the edge of the village. She lands hard in wet mud and tries to crawl backward, crying and terrified, as the daughter catches up. Do not resolve it immediately. Intercut this with the warm dream memory of the mother and child tumbling together into a field, laughing, rolling, and playing. The child climbs onto her mother playfully. They laugh, hold each other, and roll in warm grass. The cutting should now become more intimate and emotionally devastating: in one world, the daughter is on top of her like a predator; in the memory, she is on top of her like a playful child. A frightened hand in mud cuts to the same hand touching her daughter’s cheek lovingly in the warm world. A cry in the rain cuts to a laugh in golden light. Keep the sound design working with the cut structure: Present: rain, breath, wet fabric, mud, distant dogs, wind, subtle snarls or feral breathing. Memory: birds, soft wind in crops, child laughter, gentle footsteps, warm village ambience, all with a light dream-echo softness. No generated music. No score. The transitions themselves should feel musical. 0:24–0:26 — Dream Break / Infection Sting In the last two seconds, the dream fractures. The warmth collapses. Cut back hard to the cold present. Use brief disorienting flashes — the mother’s face in rain, the daughter close, the field, a trembling hand. Then give the final disturbing hint: on the mother’s neck, cheek, or temple, we glimpse subtle dark veins or infection-like changes beginning to appear. Do not show a full transformation. Just enough to suggest that now even the mother may be turning — or that the memory is collapsing into the same fate. Cut immediately. Important No dialogue needed, or only tiny involuntary cries / breaths from the mother. Let the sequence be carried by performance, camera grammar, intercutting, and ambient sound. The emotional effect should be: love memory colliding with horror reality.

promptText:
Create a highly addictive, nostalgic early-2000s Korean MiniDV home-video story designed to hook viewers within the first second and make them stay until the final reveal.

Her playful expression slowly disappears.

The camera remains completely still.

She notices something behind the old photograph: a tiny folded note.

She opens it.

Her eyes widen.

She starts laughing in disbelief while shaking her head.

The note contains a simple handwritten message:

Natural emotional reaction — not melodramatic.

SHOT 4 — 0:09–0:12 — THE EMOTIONAL TWIST

She sits silently for a moment.

Her expression becomes soft and emotional.

She looks at the old photograph again, then smiles warmly.

She gently places the photograph against her chest.

A tiny nostalgic laugh escapes.

The warm bedroom lamp creates a beautiful glow across her face while the MiniDV camera struggles slightly with exposure.

SHOT 5 — 0:12–0:15 — THE FINAL REVEAL

Suddenly she notices something written on the back of the photograph.

She flips it over.

Her eyes go wide.

She looks directly into the camera as if she has just realized something.

title: Anime Teleportation Transformation Sequence

promptText:

Role of reference images:
Image 1: Protagonist and school uniform before transformation
Image 2: Singer costume and microphone after transformation
Image 3: School classroom before disappearance
Image 4: Live stage after appearance
Image 1 and Image 2 are three-view drawings showing the same single woman from the front, side, and back, not three people. The central front view is the base, and the side and back views are used only for costume structure reference. The protagonist's face, purple-blue eyes, dark blue hair longer than the waist, hairstyle, and physique are completely maintained before and after the transformation. There is always only one character.
Before transformation: dark blue blazer, white shirt, ribbon at the chest, checkered pleated skirt, dark blue high socks, brown loafers as in Image 1. After transformation: accurately reproduce the silver-white bodice, blue crystal decorations, blue-glowing dark blue pleated skirt, iridescent transparent sleeves and long costume tail, large ribbon on the back, black-blue long boots, blue hair ornament, and blue-black microphone from Image 2.
0.0-2.2s: A deserted classroom with the setting sun shining in as in Image 3. White curtains sway heavily in the wind, and the protagonist stands alone in the center aisle between desks in her school uniform. Rapid dolly-in to the protagonist from a wide angle. The protagonist senses something and looks up. Classroom ambient sounds, wind, distant chimes.
2.2-3.5s: A blue-purple circular teleportation pattern instantly lights up at the protagonist's feet. Several thin beams of light shoot up from the floor, running rapidly through the uniform's buttons, chest ribbon, and skirt patterns. Surrounding dust and light particles are sucked toward the protagonist, and her long hair and curtains blow toward the center due to intense suction wind. The energy sound rises sharply.
3.5-4.2s: The uniform and the protagonist's outline are decomposed all at once from the outside in into countless dark blue, silver, and blue-purple light particles. The particles do not spread around the body but are compressed at ultra-high speed to a point at the chest. The uniform fabric, hair outline, and body silhouette are sucked into the light point within 0.7 seconds, and the protagonist completely disappears. Maintain the face and hair until just before disappearance, and cover the body with opaque light.
4.2-4.6s: The compressed point releases a sharp bluish-white flash, generating a reverse circular shockwave and vanishing. Papers on the desk, curtains, and dust are violently blown away by the shockwave. The protagonist is completely gone, leaving only the classroom. An afterglow momentarily floats in the air as a thin ring.
4.6-4.9s: Show the empty classroom clearly for about 0.3 seconds. Complete silence. Do not transform the background into the live stage. Do not mix the classroom and the stage. Do not show the portal or stage in advance.
[hard cut / instantaneous teleport] 4.9-5.2s: The center of the live stage in Image 4. A tiny bluish-white light point suddenly appears at the same screen coordinates where she vanished in the classroom. The stage briefly goes dark, and all lasers concentrate on the light point.
5.2-6.2s: The light point explodes into a huge spherical energy, and silver-blue particles, crystal fragments, and feathers of light are radiated at high speed in all directions. The protagonist's outline is drawn with particles in the center. The light silhouette is reconstructed in order of feet, legs, torso, arms, and long hair. Use the same color, trajectory, and rotation direction as the particles that disappeared in the classroom to clarify that the same person was teleported.
6.2-8.5s: Particles flow back into the reconstructed light silhouette. Rapidly and sequentially form the black-blue long boots, blue-glowing pleated skirt, silver-white bodice, and blue crystal decorations on the chest and shoulders from Image 2 from the feet up. Next, the iridescent transparent sleeves and long costume tail spread as a light film, and the large ribbon on the back unfolds like a flower. Do not reappear in uniform; build it up in a state converted to the singer's costume during teleportation.
8.5-9.8s: The last light particles gather at the side of the hair and are fixed as a blue crystal hair ornament. The remaining particles flow straight into the right hand, generating the blue-black microphone from Image 2 from a slender luminous outline. The moment the protagonist grips the microphone, the costume trim and crystals flash at maximum brightness.
9.8-10.5s: Transformation complete. The protagonist lands powerfully on the stage floor. Simultaneously with landing, a huge blue-purple pillar of light, a double circular shockwave, crystal fragments, star particles, and wings of light explode outward. The camera shakes briefly from the impact and immediately approaches the protagonist at high speed. Fully synchronize the heavy bass impact and crystal sounds.
10.5-12.5s: The camera revolves around the protagonist at high speed by about 180 degrees. The long dark blue hair, transparent sleeves, costume tail, and back ribbon flutter greatly due to centrifugal force. The protagonist takes a step onto the runway and raises the microphone high from her chest. An abstract blue-purple acoustic waveform runs across the large screen.
12.5-15.0s: The entire stage in Image 4 lights up explosively. Countless blue-purple lasers cross, the penlights in the audience wave all at once, and pillars of light and star particles erupt from the floor. The camera rapidly pulls back from a low position near the floor to an ultra-wide angle, showing the protagonist's entire body standing in the center of the huge stage. Finally, the protagonist looks forward and raises the microphone, and huge silver-blue wings of light open behind her. End by showing the completed costume and face clearly.
Important constraints:
Do not gradually change the background from the classroom to the stage. Do not overlap the classroom and the stage. Do not display the stage through a portal in the classroom. Strictly adhere to 'complete disappearance in the classroom -> momentary blank -> sudden appearance on the stage'. Always only one person. Do not generate three-view drawings as three people. Do not generate duplicate protagonists, expressions of another person emerging from afterimages, facial changes, hair shortening, instantaneous costume swaps, mixtures of uniforms and singer costumes, extra limbs, microphone duplicates, text, subtitles, logos, or watermarks.
Audio:
Transition from quiet classroom ambient sounds to a short, sharp energy rise sound and a suction compression sound. A sharp 'shun' sound and a moment of complete silence upon disappearance. Start a huge heavy bass, crystal sounds of particles, audience cheers, and fast-paced electronic music all at once upon appearance on the stage. No dialogue or singing.

title: Seedance 2.5 Chiropractic Product Review Video
description: A detailed product review video prompt for Seedance 2.5. It describes a documentary-style 4K video of a woman in a chiropractic clinic demonstrating a memory foam cervical pillow, including specific camera angles and a scripted storyboard.
promptText:
1. Basic Parameters
This is a vertical short video for health & home product review and recommendation, with an aspect ratio of 9:16 and a total duration of 31 seconds. The video is in 4K ultra HD, 60fps, with photorealistic portrait quality. The overall style is natural and documentary-style, lit with warm soft white light, the frame is clear and grain-free, and all camera movements are smooth and stable.

2. Fixed Scene Setting
The shooting scene is the interior of an American chiropractic clinic: the wall has a light gray matte finish, with an educational poster titled Whiplash Injuries of the Head and Neck (with head and neck anatomy illustrations) hung on the upper section of the wall. A light wood grain barn-door style storage cabinet with black metal hardware is placed against the wall, and on the countertop from left to right are a dark green cone-shaped decorative ornament, a transparent glass bottle, and a white tissue box with a blue logo. Half of an office chair with a black cushion and orange wooden legs is visible on the right side of the frame. The foreground is a dark gray leather three-section chiropractic treatment table. The entire environment is clean and tidy with even, soft lighting.

3. Fixed Character Setting
The on-screen talent is a 25-28 year old Caucasian woman with medium-length wavy blonde hair and natural, healthy skin. She wears gold round vintage earrings, a thin pearl bracelet on her left hand, and two thin plain gold rings on her left middle and ring fingers. She is dressed in a taupe brushed sports camisole (with cross straps and a drop-shaped cutout on the back) paired with matching high-waist tight yoga leggings. She has a friendly and relaxed expression, speaks in a professional yet casual tone, and all her movements are natural and unforced.

4. Core Product Setting
The core product showcased is a white ergonomic memory foam cervical pillow: it has a symmetrical cloud/plump bone shape, with curved raised support edges on the top and bottom ends, rounded bulges on the left and right sides, and a sunken central area that fits the curve of the head and neck. The pillowcase is made of skin-friendly knitted cotton with an invisible side zipper for easy removal and washing, and the inner core is slow-rebound memory foam that slowly regains its shape after being pressed, with sufficient support.

5. Storyboard Sequence
From 0 to 4 seconds, the shot is a medium static shot: the woman stands behind the treatment table, places both hands flat on the cervical pillow in the center of the table, and speaks to the camera. She gently presses down on the pillow surface to demonstrate the slow-rebound support, then lifts the pillow to chest height with both hands to show its full front outline. The corresponding voiceover is: "Today I'm sharing this amazing cervical pillow I got recommended after my chiropractic adjustment, the support is incredible."
From 4 to 5 seconds, the shot is a close-up with the camera panning slightly downward: the woman moves out of the frame, and the camera focuses on the cervical pillow on the treatment table, showing the sunken support structure from a top-down angle. There is no dialogue in this segment, only soft ambient background noise is retained.
From 5 to 8 seconds, the shot is a close-up static shot: the woman lies supine on the treatment table, with her head resting exactly in the sunken center of the pillow, her side face facing the camera. She gently shakes her head left and right to show how well the pillow conforms to her head and neck, with a relaxed expression. The corresponding voiceover is: "When you sleep on your back, your neck is fully supported, there's no gap at all."
From 8 to 12 seconds, the shot is a close-up static shot: the woman slowly rolls over to a side-lying position, with her back facing the camera and her head remaining on the pillow. This segment demonstrates that the pillow height perfectly fits the shoulder and neck during side sleeping, with no head tilt or shoulder pressure. The corresponding voiceover is: "The height is also perfect for side sleeping, it doesn't press on your shoulders at all."
From 12 to 18 seconds, the shot is a close-up static shot: the woman rolls over again to a prone position, with her chest leaning lightly on the pillow, her face resting sideways on the center of the pillow surface, and her arms wrapping around the pillow. She closes her eyes with a comfortable and relaxed expression, and her voice is slightly muffled to match the prone position. The corresponding voiceover is: "It's even super comfortable to rest on when you're scrolling on your phone lying on your stomach."
From 18 to 28 seconds, the shot is a medium static shot: the woman gets up and stands back behind the treatment table, holds the pillow upright with both hands, points to the raised structures of different heights on the side of the pillow and the invisible zipper with her right fingertip in turn, and repeatedly flips the pillow to show the layered side design while explaining. The corresponding voiceover is: "The two sides have different heights: the higher side is great for back sleeping to support your cervical spine, the lower side is perfect for side sleeping. The pillowcase has a zipper so you can wash it, and the memory foam has really great support."
From 28 to 31 seconds, the shot is a medium static shot: the woman places the pillow steadily back in the center of the treatment table, lets her hands hang naturally by her sides, and smiles and nods at the camera as the closing. The corresponding voiceover is: "If you have neck issues, you have to try this, it's a total game changer."

6. Negative Constraints
Facial distortion and misaligned facial features are prohibited; pillow shape deformation and proportion distortion are prohibited; scene prop errors and garbled text on posters are prohibited; shaky camera and blurry frames are prohibited; stiff character movements and exaggerated expressions are prohibited; color distortion and abrupt filters are prohibited.

title: Anime Character Good Morning Wake-up

promptText:
INPUT
Use the attached reference image as the first frame of the video.

FORMAT
20 seconds, 24fps. No BGM. Only quiet indoor ambient sounds. Soft breathing sounds, rustling of clothes, and the faint sound of hands touching the floor.

CAMERA LOCK
Camera is completely fixed. No panning, tilting, zooming, or movement. One take. The angle only changes when the character themselves moves closer to the lens.

FOCUS RULE
The focus is always on her body movements. No time is spent describing the background, light, or space. Ensure the screen is held by what she is doing at every moment. No single action lasts more than 3 seconds. Must move to the next action within 3 seconds. No moments of complete stillness.

IDENTITY LOCK
Do not change the face, hairstyle, hair color, eyes, or clothing from the first frame. Do not turn her into a different person.

VISUAL STYLE
Maintain the color tone, contrast, depth of field, and texture of the first frame throughout. Do not change the direction or intensity of the lighting.

TIMELINE

0.0-2.0s
The head drops forward and then lifts up with a start. The hair sways slightly delayed.

2.0-4.0s
Rub one eye with the back of a clenched fist. Rub the other eye as well.

4.0-6.0s
A small stretch. The body leans to the side and then returns.

6.0-8.0s
Eyes meet the lens. The neck tilts, and the upper body follows. The mouth opens slightly.

8.0-10.0s
Place both hands on the floor in front, leaning the upper body forward. Hair falls forward from the shoulders.

10.0-16.0s
Crawls towards the lens on all fours. One hand at a time, the upper body swaying left and right with each movement. Hair sways beside the face. The face gradually gets larger in the frame. While approaching, eyes remain fixed on the lens.

16.0-18.0s
Super close-up. The face occupies most of the screen. Corners of the mouth lift, eyes narrow, and says "Good morning" in a bright, bouncy voice.

18.0-20.0s
Backed away slightly. Eyes narrow into crescents, nose wrinkles, and cheeks lift. Shoulders sway slightly. Remains in that expression.

NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS
Camera movement, zoom, and pan prohibited. No cuts. No periods of complete stillness. Prohibit single actions lasting more than 3 seconds. Prohibit using duration for background or scene descriptions. Poses, peace signs, winks, and blowing kisses prohibited. Quick or jumping movements prohibited. Standing up prohibited. Changing character identity prohibited. Real-life style conversion prohibited. No speech other than "Good morning".

title: Xianxia Cold Comedy Short Film

promptText:
Seedance | 15-second Deadpan Comedy Short | "The Fourth One"

I. Mission Objective
Generate a complete and continuous 15-second Chinese Xianxia (fantasy) movie short.

Overall Style Requirements:
Cinematic realistic texture
Pure ancient Chinese Xianxia aesthetics
Deconstruct the epic "avenger's entrance" pressure into a serious survival-type comedy
Restrained deadpan performance
Silent film-style reaction rhythm
Classic "three-beat progression"
Clear status reversal
Arri Alexa cinematic texture
Stable and clear facial micro-details
Fine film grain
Natural volumetric light

II. Core Comedy Logic
Keep only one easy-to-understand main line:
An enemy enters aggressively to avenge three brothers who have already lost, proudly identifying himself as the "fourth challenger."
Until the Master casually asks a very ordinary question, he suddenly realizes: he is the last one in his sect who can still stand and come to challenge.

Humor Sources:
Delayed reaction (belated realization)
A normal person's survival instinct
Serious dialogue rhythm
The character gradually realizing the problem himself
Prohibitions:
Character suddenly becoming stupid
Random environmental accidents
Exaggerated slapstick performance

III. Reference Anchors
Character Anchors
@Image 1: Character ID A | Sword Immortal Senior Sister
@Image 2: Character ID B | Junior Sister

Environmental DNA
All newly uploaded background and location reference images determine a single set of environmental DNA. Before formal composition, silently integrate and reconstruct compatible:
Real terrain, architectural language, spatial scale, vegetation, water bodies, weather, mountain mist, main light direction, reflection relationships, atmospheric depth, real walkable paths.
Environment Principles:
Water, mist, vegetation, fabrics, and distant ambient sounds must continue natural movement. The environment must remain Neutral in narrative: no active gags, no plot triggering, no reversal pushing, no interruption of character rhythm.

IV. Character Settings
Character ID A | Sword Immortal Senior Sister | @Image 1
Always the same 25-30 year old East Asian female: Tall and slender, oval face, dark almond eyes, long black hair half-up, fixed with a white jade hairpin, white embroidered silk Hanfu, semi-transparent layered wide sleeves, silver waist seal, jade pendant, white cloth boots, a single silver long sword.
Character Temperament: Calm, restrained, never exaggerated, handles challengers like daily sect chores.

Character ID B | Junior Sister | @Image 2
Always the same 20-25 year old East Asian female: Small build, round and lively face, black hair braided, cyan-green linen Hanfu, dark belt, wooden hairpin, black cloth shoes, a single dark steel sword.
Character Temperament: Quick reflexes, accurate comedic judgment, concise retorts, restrained but readable expressions.

Character C | Enemy Swordsman
An angry enemy swordsman enters with great momentum, viewing himself as a hero coming for revenge. Very oppressive in the first half, gradually realizing he shouldn't be fighting in the second half, eventually turning from an "avenger" to the "only surviving challenger."

Character D | Master
Same elderly Master, standing a few steps behind the two, serving as a quiet witness. Minimal lines, but one sentence completes the core reversal, followed by a final light verbal jab.

V. 15-second Three-Shot Structure
Shot 1 | 0–5s | Wide / Long Shot | Avenger's Entrance
In the open area naturally planned according to the reference images: same white-robed Senior Sister, same green-robed Junior Sister, same Master. Spatial relationship is stable. An angry enemy swordsman strides into the frame. He draws his sword with a "clang" and announces heroically: "I come to avenge my three senior brothers!" The white-robed Sister is not nervous at all, calmly asking: "Which three?" The enemy immediately replies: "The one who fell in the water, the one hanging in the tree, and the one who rolled down the mountain, they are all my brothers!"

Shot 2 | 5–10s | Medium / Cowboy Shot | The meaning of "The Fourth" changes
Maintain all characters, costumes, and the identical geographic space. The Junior Sister finally recognizes him and says: "Oh, you're the fourth one." The enemy instantly straightens up and proudly replies: "Correct!" He must not hear any problem, even becoming more proud. Then the focus shifts to the Master who asks casually: "How many disciples does your master have left?" The enemy answers instinctively without thinking: "... Just me." After speaking, there must be a beat of absolute silence. Don't cut away quickly. Keep the transformation on the enemy's face: heroic aura still hanging there, brain one beat late to react, then realizing what that sentence meant. The Junior Sister looks at his drawn sword, then back at him, asking naturally: "Are you still fighting?"

Shot 3 | 10–15s | Close-up / Extreme Close-up | Survival instinct defeats revenge
Maintain all characters and relations. The enemy looks at the Sister, then the Junior Sister, and finally down at the sword in his hand. He begins to seriously calculate the consequences. Then he very slowly sheathes the sword, saying in a suddenly mature tone: "Wait for Master to recruit two more." Complete half-beat pause. The Sister actually nods to him formally, as if approving a true martial judgment: "Progressing." The Junior Sister adds: "Mostly he learned how to calculate." Focus on Master who nods seriously: "At least this trip wasn't in vain." Then extreme close-up. The enemy tries to maintain his last bit of dignity and turns to leave. After two steps, he stops without looking back, whispering: "My three brothers... they are all still alive, right?" The Sister answers almost instantly: "Alive." The enemy's shoulders show a visible, physical relaxation. Then he leaves with a noticeably faster pace. The Junior Sister watches his back and sighs: "This sect finally produced a cautious one." Finally, in the background, the Master hides a tiny smile as it cuts to black.

VI. Performance Requirements
Senior Sister: Never exaggerated, calm as if handling daily chores, formally acknowledging the enemy's retreat.
Junior Sister: Quick reactions, stable comedic timing, naturally delivered lines.
Enemy: First half full of avenger's momentum; middle transition shows the slow collapse of the heroic narrative; second half shows survival instinct and trying to keep face.
Master: Minimal lines, casual tone but accurate, extremely subtle final smile.

VII. Cinematography and Tone
15 seconds total, 16:9 horizontal, three continuous clear shots. Native Mandarin dialogue, precise lip-sync, clear comedic pauses. Arri Alexa look, stable sharp facial details, natural volumetric lighting. Restrained camera movement, stable shots, giving time for reactions to land.

VIII. Continuity

title: Indian Village Football Documentary
description: A handheld MiniDV style documentary prompt capturing the daily life and joy of a young girl playing football in an Indian village.
promptText: Create an ultra-realistic Indian village documentary sequence shot entirely on an old handheld MiniDV / Hi8-style camcorder, following a young village girl who plays football every day with the local kids. Everything should feel observational and slightly amateur, like a small documentary crew has been following her life for a few days and she has become comfortable with the cameraman. Slightly faded colors, baked-in camcorder sharpness, mild interlacing, tape softness, compression noise, autofocus hunting, exposure pumping, rough handheld movement, imperfect zooms, accidental reframing, operator footsteps, wind hitting the microphone, children shouting in the distance, village ambience, birds, dogs, and natural location audio. No music. No modern cinematic grading. No gimbal. No dramatic sports-commercial photography. The camera should feel physically carried by one person. The setting is a real Indian village football ground: not a professional pitch, just an open dusty field between houses and farmland, uneven patches of grass, stones marking boundaries, homemade goalposts, children in ordinary clothes, a few slippers and bags lying near the side, bicycles nearby, villagers occasionally watching from the edge. Shot 1 — She takes the documentary crew to the ground Start with the cameraman already following the young Indian girl footballer through a narrow village lane. She walks slightly ahead of the camera carrying or lightly kicking her old football, completely natural and comfortable with the documentary crew. She turns around while still walking and says in English with a natural Indian accent: “Come with me. I’ll show you where we play football every day.” The cameraman follows behind her with slightly shaky footsteps. She walks out of the lane and onto the open field. She spreads her hand toward the rough football ground and proudly says: “This is it.” Do not make the reveal grand or cinematic. The charm is that she is incredibly proud of a very ordinary dusty village field. Shot 2 — The joy of playing Cut to the cameraman already standing close to the edge of the game while the children are playing. The same girl runs past the camera chasing the ball with other village kids. The camera operator struggles to follow them, performs a clumsy little pan, briefly loses focus, then catches them again. The cameraman laughs from behind the camera and says in English with a natural Indian accent: “See how much fun this is?” The girl glances toward him while still moving, grins, and immediately runs back into play. Keep this shot energetic and documentary-real: children shouting things like “Pass! Pass!”, feet kicking dust, someone nearly running into the camera, the operator stepping aside, an imperfect zoom toward the ball, then quickly widening again because the action changes direction. Shot 3 — Bicycle-kick goal and celebration Cut to what feels like the final moments of the same village match. The camera is handheld from the sideline, slightly too far away, trying to follow the action. Several kids rush toward the makeshift goal. One player near the side sends a high crossing ball into the middle. The cameraman reacts late and pans quickly. The same girl runs into position, watches the descending ball, turns her body— and performs a completely believable bicycle kick. Her back leaves the ground, one leg swings upward, she connects cleanly with the ball in midair, and the ball flies toward the makeshift goal. The goalkeeper reacts— goal. The children immediately explode in celebration. No slow motion. No heroic cinematic cutaway. Let the old camcorder almost miss the kick because the operator is trying desperately to keep up. The girl jumps back to her feet and starts running directly toward the documentary camera, yelling in English: “YEEEAAAH!” Her teammates chase behind her, screaming and celebrating. She reaches the camera laughing, nearly filling the lens, jumping around with the others as the operator backs away and struggles to keep everyone framed. Kids hug her, slap her hands, shout, jump, and crowd around the camera in exactly the messy way children celebrate after scoring. The lens briefly loses focus because everyone is too close. End inside that chaos — her laughing directly toward the cameraman while the other children are still celebrating around her. Overall feeling: a tiny observational documentary about an ordinary village girl suddenly becoming a football hero for one moment. It should feel warm, real, imperfect, spontaneous and completely unstaged — the camera just happened to be there when she scored the best goal of the match.

title: Surreal Desert Mirror Fantasy
description: A surreal cinematic dark fantasy prompt featuring two knights arriving at a giant circular mirror in a desert that reflects a futuristic city.
promptText: SUBJECT ANCHOR 1: <<<image_1>>> — Ash Knight SUBJECT ANCHOR 2: <<<image_2>>> — Obsidian Rival PROP ANCHOR: <<<image_3>>> — Magma Greatsword DURATION: 30 seconds ASPECT RATIO: 16:9 STYLE: Surreal cinematic dark fantasy / science-fantasy CAMERA: Large-format cinema, 24mm / 35mm / 50mm / 85mm FRAME RATE: 24fps with selective 60fps STORY In the middle of an endless desert stands a gigantic circular mirror buried vertically in the sand. Ash Knight arrives from one direction. Obsidian Rival arrives from another. The mirror does not reflect them. Instead, it shows a completely different version of the desert—one thousands of years in the future. --- 00:00–00:05 — THE DESERT Open with an enormous aerial shot of an endless black-and-gold desert at sunset. Wind creates long patterns across the dunes. At the center of the landscape stands a gigantic circular metallic structure half-buried in the sand. The camera descends toward it. Ash Knight appears as a distant silhouette walking across the dunes. --- 00:05–00:09 — THE SECOND ARRIVAL Cut to a 50mm side profile. Ash Knight reaches the structure. Across the enormous circular mirror, Obsidian Rival emerges from the opposite side. Both stop. The mirror stands between them. The camera slowly moves sideways, keeping the entire structure centered. --- 00:09–00:13 — THE MIRROR 85mm close-up. The surface of the mirror is perfectly black. Ash Knight approaches it. His reflection should appear— but it doesn't. Instead, the mirror shows the same location thousands of years later. The desert has disappeared. A massive futuristic city now covers the landscape. --- 00:13–00:17 — THE FUTURE 35mm composition. Obsidian Rival steps closer. The mirror changes again. It shows a completely different future. The city is now empty. Towering structures are covered in sand. A gigantic red moon hangs above the horizon. The two warriors look toward the impossible reflection. --- 00:17–00:21 — THE SWORD 85mm macro. Ash Knight draws the Magma Greatsword. The red lava veins pulse. The mirror responds. A thin red reflection appears across its surface. The reflection of the sword suddenly becomes visible even though the warriors still have no reflections. --- 00:21–00:25 — THE FRACTURE Ash Knight slowly raises the Greatsword toward the mirror. He does not strike. The mirror surface begins developing thin luminous cracks by itself. The cracks spread outward like a massive geometric pattern. The desert wind suddenly stops. Every grain of sand becomes completely still. --- 00:25–00:28 — THE OTHER WORLD The mirror opens like a doorway. Beyond it is not another desert. It is an enormous ocean suspended vertically in the sky. Massive floating structures drift beneath the water. The camera slowly pushes forward. Both warriors remain behind the threshold. --- 00:28–00:30 — FINAL IMAGE Extreme wide shot. The circular mirror now stands open in the middle of the desert. Inside it, the impossible ocean-world stretches endlessly. Ash Knight and Obsidian Rival stand on opposite sides of the opening. The Magma Greatsword glows faintly. A single wave moves across the vertical ocean. The mirror suddenly closes. The desert returns to normal. CUT TO BLACK. No text. No title. No logo. CHARACTER CONTINUITY Preserve the exact reference appearance throughout. Ash Knight: exact armor, magma rune patterns, cape, proportions, silhouette and identity. Obsidian Rival: exact obsidian dragon-scale armor, horned helmet, orange visor, proportions, silhouette and identity. Magma Greatsword: exact blade geometry, jagged edges, handle, forged texture and red lava veins. No redesigns, identity drift, morphing, duplicates, weapon transformation, armor changes or flickering. ENVIRONMENT CONTINUITY One desert. One circular mirror. Same sunset. Same sand. Same weather. Same positions of the characters. The mirror's internal worlds may change, but the physical desert remains consistent. CINEMATOGRAPHY 24mm — vast desert. 35mm — character/environment compositions. 50mm — dramatic character shots. 85mm — mirror and sword details. Slow aerial descent. Lateral tracking. Controlled push-ins. Smooth crane movement. Subtle 60fps during the mirror fracture. Natural motion blur. Realistic sand interaction. Large-format cinematic depth. VISUAL DESIGN Golden desert. Deep blue-black shadows. Warm sunset. Black reflective mirror. Red magma glow. Cold futuristic architecture inside the mirror. Surreal vertical ocean. The color palette should evolve naturally rather than remaining monochromatic. NEGATIVE PROMPT text, subtitles, watermark, logo, modern clothing, cartoon, anime, low-poly, plastic armor, character redesign, identity drift, face morphing, weapon redesign, duplicate characters, extra limbs, malformed hands, inconsistent proportions, flickering, random camera movement, environment reset, inconsistent lighting, excessive destruction, graphic gore, blood, dismemberment, blurry subjects, flat lighting. DIRECTOR'S NOTE: Do not explain the mirror. The audience should discover its rules visually. The first reveal establishes that it shows the future; the second reveal breaks that assumption; the final reveal shows an entirely impossible world. The ending should leave the viewer with a question rather than an answer.

title: Dark Fantasy Queen Monster Transformation
description: A comprehensive cinematic prompt for a 30-second continuous shot featuring a queen transforming into a monster and hunting a soldier in a grand palace.
promptText: Ultra-realistic AAA live-action dark fantasy film. 30 seconds of completely continuous single-camera, uncut long-take. Maintains strict spatial coordinates and time axis, expressing depth of field and heavy atmosphere comparable to ARRI ALEXA 65. Environment: (Ref 3) huge royal palace. Black/white/gold marble floor, volumetric light from stained glass, huge chandelier. Soldiers in silver, gold, and dark blue military uniforms are crowded on the left and right. Queen: (Ref 1) beautiful queen. Long platinum-blonde hair, golden crown with blue jewels, royal dress of white to ivory with gold embroidery and dark blue. Queen (Monster Form): (Ref 2) huge monstrosity. Retains the crown and platinum hair, has multi-layered fangs, long claws, and bone-membrane organs on the back. Sinner: (Ref 4) male soldier. Brown hair, dirt and wounds, silver-gold armor, dark blue costume, handcuffs and chains. 0.0-4.5s: Camera starts from behind the queen. Queen's back in foreground, sinner about 12m ahead in central aisle, rows of soldiers on left and right. Guard pushes sinner forward, sinner is slammed onto marble on both knees. Camera passes by the queen's right shoulder, continuously advancing toward the sinner to capture the upper chest. <Low impact sound of heavy armor colliding with floor, sharp metallic sound of chains> Sinner looks up and says in an urgent voice. {Your Majesty... please forgive me!} 4.5-9.5s: Camera doesn't stop, passes left side of sinner, draws a smooth arc to capture queen on the throne side from the front. Queen steps forward. Queen says in a quiet, cold voice. {Did you think you could steal the royal treasure and escape?} <Dry metallic sound of soldiers reaching for sword hilts simultaneously> Sinner shouts. {No! I—} Queen takes another step, emotion disappears from face. 9.5-14.4s: Camera approaches queen by about 1m. Queen's skeleton and muscles continuously deform under skin, corners of mouth tear, multi-layered fangs are exposed. Platinum hair flutters, bone-membrane organs expand from back. Body enlarges, transforming into monster form while dress tears. <Skeletal deformation sounds, meat stretching sounds> Monster queen roars. <Unusual roar that makes stained glass resonate> Soldiers on left and right drop to one knee in a wave. Sinner says while backing away. {No way...!} 14.4-19.6s: Sinner turns 180 degrees and begins sprinting at full speed toward camera (palace interior direction). From here, camera continues to retreat along central aisle toward palace interior. Fixed linear relationship: "Camera ← Sinner ← Monster Queen ← Throne". Monster queen begins chase on all fours. Sinner shouts behind while running. {Stop! Don't come!} <Rough breathing, armor sound, heavy impact sound of monster's huge limbs hitting marble> Sinner's chain gets caught on marble decoration, sinner collapses forward. Camera also slows retreat. 19.6-23.4s: Camera almost stops on current central aisle. Monster queen catches up from behind, blocks escape route with right forelimb. Monster's neck extends, huge jaws grab sinner's torso from diagonal rear and lift him up. <Metallic crushing sound, short scream, sound of chain breaking and falling to floor> Monster queen moves jaws and completely swallows sinner. Sinner's body completely disappears from screen. 23.4-30.0s: Monster queen does not move from that predation position (away from throne), begins de-transformation into human form. Bone organs are folded, body shrinks, torn dress is restored with golden magical threads. Camera retreats very slowly by about 1m. <Skeletal contraction sounds, delicate sounds of costume restoration> Queen, fully returned to human form, fixes slightly tilted crown near chains on floor. Surrounding soldiers stand up. A new sinner is pulled out from back of screen. Queen stares at new sinner and says coldly. {Next.} Camera retreats/rises further down central aisle, ending with new sinner in foreground, queen in center, and throne in background. [Continuity & Spatial Constraints] Maintain continuous long-take with a single physical camera for 30 seconds. After 14.4 seconds, camera only retreats toward palace interior. Monster queen always stays behind sinner. After predation, sinner's body remains completely disappeared. Queen remains at the spot where she completed predation and does not return to throne. During de-transformation, camera only retreats maintaining axis on current central aisle, actions like circling queen or moving to front are strictly prohibited.

title: Realistic Wing Chun Kung Fu Training Video
description: A professional prompt for a 20-second high-speed Wing Chun martial arts video, focusing on precise hand techniques and the iconic one-inch punch.
promptText: [Style] Photorealistic Wing Chun Film, high-energy Douyin action video, Ramp-mo rhythm transitions, High-Speed Photography, 4K cinematic quality, realistic skin, sweat, and wood textures, no anime feel, no magic effects. [Duration] 20 seconds. [Aspect Ratio] 9:16 vertical screen. [Scene] Traditional old Lingnan martial arts hall, dark wood floors, mottled gray walls, wooden lattice windows; morning sunlight streaming in from the side, tiny dust motes floating in the air. A traditional solid wood wooden dummy is fixed in the center of the frame, with a cylindrical body, three wooden arms, and one slanted wooden leg. [Character] Wing Chun practitioner as per Image 1. Face, features, hairstyle, body proportions, and original clothing must strictly follow the image, maintaining the same person and look throughout. [Audio] No dialogue, no subtitles; emphasize the sound of dummy collisions, footsteps rubbing, short breaths, and the sound of wood splintering at the end. [00:00-00:04] Shot 1: Opening high-speed dummy striking (Impact Hook). The first frame enters high-speed action directly without environmental setup. Close-up side shot: The protagonist is rapidly practicing on the wooden dummy, hands continuously performing Tan Sau, Bong Sau, Pak Sau, palm strikes, and short punches around the centerline; hands switch rapidly between the three wooden arms, causing the arms to vibrate continuously. The camera tracks horizontally close to the protagonist's hands (Close Tracking), with hands flashing past the lens with natural motion blur; each strike produces different wood sounds. Cut to a low-angle full-body shot: The protagonist uses tight small steps to bypass the slanted leg of the dummy, upper body remains stable, feet do not cross, no large jumps. The final palm strike lands heavily in the center, the whole dummy shakes violently, dust falls, but no cracks appear. [00:04-00:08] Shot 2: Sudden deceleration · Precise slow practice (Ramp Down). After the final strike, all sound suddenly goes quiet, transitioning to slow motion. Side-front medium shot: The protagonist slows down, left hand against the upper arm, slowly dissolving outward; right hand delivers a short straight punch along the center of the dummy, retracting quickly after contact. The protagonist continues slowly performing Bong Sau, Pak Sau, and palm strikes, each movement clearly separated, arms short and close to the body, elbows not excessively flared. The camera orbits the protagonist and dummy about 90 degrees (Slow Orbit), showing the palm brushing the rough wood grain, slight vibration of the wooden arms, and sweat dripping down the cheek. The protagonist's gaze is locked on the center of the dummy, shoulders relaxed, lips slightly closed, breathing steady; observing distance and rhythm rather than angry flailing. [00:08-00:12] Shot 3: Slow to fast · Progressive acceleration. Low drum beats enter, the practice speed increases layer by layer. First set: Moderate speed, left hand dissolves arm, right palm strikes center. Second set: Visibly faster, Bong Sau to Pak Sau, followed by two short punches. Third set: Highest speed, left and right hands alternate rapidly, punches and palms crossing along the centerline, combined with small turns and ground-hugging footwork to the side of the dummy. Low-angle Steadicam Orbit from behind to the side-front; foreground wooden arms flash past, background windows and sunlight form slight speed trails. Movement gets faster, but the body doesn't sway, face remains steady, only breathing becomes heavier and gaze more focused. The dummy vibrates constantly with dense wood sounds, remaining intact. [00:12-00:14] Shot 4: Sudden stop · Locking on the dummy (Sudden Silence). After the high-speed combo, hands suddenly stop. All drums, strikes, and camera movement stop simultaneously. Fixed front medium shot: The protagonist stands before the dummy, feet unmoving, left hand retracted to chest, right hand hanging naturally. The dummy is still vibrating slightly, a few wood chips fall. Close-up of face: The protagonist slowly lifts eyes, locking gaze on the center of the dummy; lips tighten slightly, taking a deep breath. The scene remains quiet, pausing for the final one-inch punch. [00:14-00:17] Shot 5: Open palm approach · Clenching fist to store energy (Open Palm to Fist). Side medium-close shot: The protagonist slowly raises the right hand, fingers fully spread, palm facing the center of the dummy. Must clearly show a fully open palm first, not a fist. title: Emotional Bedroom Dialogue Scene
description: A detailed 30-second cinematic prompt focusing on vulnerability and fear between a couple in a bedroom setting, featuring specific character reactions and lighting instructions.
promptText:
[PROJECT TYPE] Text-to-video. 30-second dialogue scene. Vulnerability and fear.

[Global Setting] Modern bedroom at night. Soft warm lamplight. Both lying in bed. 
Intimate but vulnerable atmosphere. Quiet, introspective setting.

[Character 1  The Woman] Mid-30s, dark long hair, wearing soft shirt. Calm but 
visibly carrying emotional weight. Eyes reflect vulnerability and fear.

[Character 2 The Man] Mid-30s, short dark hair, wearing casual shirt. Warm 
expression, patient, listening presence.

[Opening, 0–3s] Wide shot of bedroom. Both lying in bed facing each other, close 
but not touching yet. Woman stares at him with fear in her eyes. Long pause. She 
takes a breath and says quietly: "I'm scared you're going to leave me." Her voice 
is small, trembling, raw with vulnerability. Man doesn't respond immediately 
just holds her gaze.

[Reaction Moment, 3–10s] Man's expression softens with tenderness. He reaches out 
slowly and touches her face with his hand, thumb brushing her cheek gently. He 
says quietly but firmly: "I'm not going anywhere." Woman's eyes fill with tears. 
He continues: "I promise." His voice is steady, certain, safe. Woman nods slightly, 
tears falling.

[Connection, 10–20s] Man moves closer, pulls her into his chest. Woman wraps her 
arms around him, holding tight. They hold each other in silence for a moment. 
Then she whispers into his chest: "Don't ever leave me." Man responds softly, 
into her hair: "Never. I've got you." He holds her tighter. Both breathing slowly, 
finding calm in each other's presence. Lamplight catches their faces  vulnerable 
but safe.

[Final Moment, 20–30s] They pull back slightly to face each other again. Woman's 
tears are still visible but her breathing is calmer. Man wipes her tears gently 
with his thumb. He looks directly into her eyes and says softly: "You're safe with 
me. Always." Woman nods, fear slowly releasing from her face, replaced by trust. 
She leans forward and kisses him soft, tender, vulnerable. They hold the kiss 
for a moment. Pull back slightly, foreheads touching, both eyes closed. Breathing 
together in shared safety and love.

[Audio] Soft ambient sound  gentle breathing, heartbeats subtle underneath, 
barely perceptible, intimate. Maybe one sustained soft string note or piano pad. 
Very minimal. Mostly silence and breathing. The quiet is sacred. No dialogue 
overlap space between words.

[Tone] Intimate, tender, vulnerable but safe. Fear acknowledged and met with love. 
Deep emotional connection. This is about being truly seen and accepted at your 
most fragile.

[Consistency]
— Same couple throughout
— Warm soft bedroom lighting
— Intimate bed setting
— Emotions: fear → acceptance → safety → trust
— Physical connection: eye contact → touch → embrace → forehead touch
— Both equally vulnerable and present

title: Supernatural Assassin Fortress Infiltration
description: A high-end Hollywood action prompt for a stealthy assassin infiltration featuring supernatural phase-dodge effects.
promptText:
Duration: 14 Seconds | Aspect Ratio: 16:9
STYLE: Ultra-photorealistic REAL LIVE-ACTION, AAA Hollywood supernatural assassin action, premium realistic Semi-CGI VFX, ARRI ALEXA 65, IMAX, Panavision anamorphic. Fast controlled choreography, brief micro slow-motion ONLY for phase-dodge.

CHARACTER: @Image1 = KAIA. Preserve exact face, hairstyle, body proportions and ORIGINAL CLOTHING. TWIN CURVED DAGGERS. Personality: COLD, FOCUSED, EFFICIENT, UNHURRIED—never frantic.

LOCATION: Night atop a snowbound mountain fortress: stone battlements, frost-slick walkways, watchtowers, torch braziers under a full moon. Sentries patrol separately. Fortress stays quiet—NO alarm, crowd, or large battle.

00:00–00:03 — SILENT HUNT

Camera already moving, low handheld pursuit behind Kaia as she crosses a frosted walkway. Two sentries patrol ahead along the battlement. She waits, motionless in shadow, until one turns his back.

WHOOM— short burst of SWIRLING SNOW-ASH. Kaia's REAL BODY physically accelerates past him, trailing translucent frost-grey afterimages. She stops at blade range behind him.

SHK-SHK— TWO precise dagger strikes. She catches and quietly lowers him. The second sentry begins turning—Kaia is already gone.

00:03–00:06 — BLIND SPOT

Camera slides around a watchtower as the second sentry scans the dark, breath visible in the cold. Kaia silently emerges from his blind spot, pins his weapon arm—

SHK-SHK. TWO precise strikes. She quietly lowers him and looks toward three sentries near the gatehouse, expression unreadable.

00:06–00:08 — PHASE-DODGE

Kaia crosses silently behind the gatehouse sentries. One unexpectedly notices and swings at her FROM BEHIND.

Camera rushes toward the incoming blade—MICRO SLOW-MOTION. Just before impact, Kaia's physical body visibly DISSOLVES into DRIFTING SNOW-ASH and pale moonlit vapor. The blade passes harmlessly THROUGH her swirling form.

TIME SNAP—WHOOSH! The ash sweeps around the attacker as camera performs a curved whip-pan. Kaia visibly REFORMS directly behind him—feet → torso → arms → face → TWIN DAGGERS.

He turns too late.

CROSS-SLASH. ONE precise counter. Tiny camera impact bump. Kaia catches and silently lowers him.

00:08–00:11 — ASSASSIN CHAIN

Two sentries remain. Kaia disappears behind a brazier instead of charging.

One passes—snow-ash curls behind him. Kaia emerges: TWO STRIKES, catches him, then slips back into shadow.

Final sentry sees a fading translucent afterimage and follows it, sword raised. Camera rotates around him—the REAL Kaia is already in his blind spot.

SHK-SHK. ONE controlled exchange. She catches and quietly lowers the FINAL SENTRY.

ALL ENEMIES ARE DEFEATED. NONE REMAIN.

00:11–00:14 — SILENT AFTERMATH

Absolute quiet. Camera tracks backward along the battlement, slower than before. All defeated sentries lie silently along Kaia's infiltration path. Braziers still burn; gates remain intact; NO alarm.

Kaia calmly wipes her TWIN DAGGERS and sheathes them.

CLICK.

Her eyes shift toward distant torchlight. Snow-ash curls around her feet.

WHOOM— Kaia silently bursts into the storm. Camera rushes after her but catches only translucent frost-grey afterimages fading into the blizzard, then holds on empty, drifting snow.

END.

CORE ASSASSIN LOGIC

OBSERVE → BLIND SPOT → SILENT APPROACH → PRECISE STRIKE → CONTROL FALL → DISENGAGE → NEXT TARGET.

Never frontal brawling or prolonged blade exchanges.

PHASE-DODGE: Incoming attack → micro slow-motion → blade almost connects → Kaia visibly dissolves into snow-ash → attack passes through → ash travels around attacker → Kaia visibly reforms at blind spot → precise counter. Use ONLY when directly attacked; do not spam.

VFX / CAMERA / AUDIO

Speed VFX: Drifting snow-ash + pale moonlit vapor + translucent frost-grey afterimages. During normal bursts, REAL Kaia always physically leads; VFX trails behind. Phase-dodge requires visible dissolve → ash travel → physical reformation. NO lightning, electrical arcs, or teleportation.

Camera: NEVER static. Low pursuit, over-shoulder stalking, watchtower reveals, close reactions, reactive whip-pans, curved tracking. FAST during eliminations, immediately CALM afterward: QUIET → FAST → QUIET → FAST → QUIET.

Audio: Wind, distant howling, torch crackle, soft footsteps on snow, fabric movement, subtle ash WHOOSH, dagger draw/impact, controlled body movement. No loud battle music or alarms.

NEGATIVE: No frontal mass battle, prolonged blade exchange, running fight, lightning/electricity, teleportation, excessive phase-dodge, explosions/destruction, static camera, robotic movement, air-gap dagger hits, surviving enemies, face/body/clothing/dagger drift, broken anatomy, full-3D/game look, subtitles, logo, watermark.

[Character Performance Curve] Character emotions must change naturally with the competition: Start: Beautiful, confident, relaxed → Rollers: Starting to get tense, but still handling it well → Pendulum Bridge: Obvious clumsiness, panic, genuine fall → Re-standing: Refusing to lose, continuing the sprint → High Wall: Fatigued, giving everything → Grabbing wall top: Excitement at 'finally having a chance to succeed' → Hooking wall top: Tense, exerting force, near limit → Successful flip: Brief disbelief → Pressing finish button: Complete confirmation of success → End: Surprise, relief, pride, happiness. Character is not a professional athlete-style perfect performance. Overall maintains natural body reactions of a real ordinary adult challenger participating in a large-scale entertainment competition. Even with final success, the character's movements must retain real fatigue, clumsiness, gasping, slight stumbles, and on-the-spot reactions. [Sound Design] Retain real large-scale TV sports entertainment show on-site sounds throughout. Including: Starting buzzer, real-time audience cheers, applause, gasps, on-site laughter, live commentary, character's running footsteps, mechanical roller rotation sounds, pendulum mechanical axis operation sounds, air sounds of pendulums sweeping quickly, soft thud of soft pendulums hitting the body, platform contact sound of the character falling on the narrow bridge, character's heavy breathing, wall stepping sounds, friction sound of hands grabbing the wall edge, friction of clothing against the wall top when flipping, finish button press sound, success signal buzzer sound, on-site timing stop. Live commentary must change in real-time based on character's actions. When a pendulum hits the character and causes a fall, the audience clearly gasps. When the character stands back up, cheers resume with continuous encouragement. When character grabs the wall top, cheers rise rapidly. When character successfully hooks her knee, commentary tone becomes obviously excited. When character flips over the wall, the entire venue erupts in huge cheers. After the finish button is pressed, cheers, applause, and the success buzzer reach their peak together. BGM is a tense instrumental score with the atmosphere of a large Japanese sports entertainment special. Gradually intensifies with the competition progress. Enters the most tense segment when the character grabs the wall top. Forms a clear, soaring victory climax when flipping successfully and pressing the button. [Cinematography Rules] Employs real large-scale TV competition show multi-camera live logic. Shots prioritize: where the character is, what the obstacle is, how the character is passing, why the collision happened, and how the character completes the final challenge. Wide shots establish obstacle space. Mid-long shots show full actions. Side track shots cover running and movement. Low water-level shots reinforce pendulum size and bridge height. Fixed side-angle obstacle cameras clearly show pendulum trajectories, character dodging, and collision processes. Telephoto covers character's tense expressions and the final wall sprint. ENG mid-close shots cover character's clumsy reactions, falling, re-standing, and wall-top exertion. Finish platform close-ups cover the button press and final victory expression. Camera cuts are natural and sharp, maintaining real TV show hard-cut rhythm. Cut frequency naturally increases as the competition enters the latter half. Each cut must continue the character's body posture, movement direction, location, and progress from the previous shot. [Final Mandatory Constraints] Full story sequence must be strictly maintained: 1. Character Debut: Leg close-up → Upper body → Face → Smile → Clench fist. 2. Roller Obstacle: Slight loss of balance occurs, but passed successfully. 3. Pendulum Narrow Bridge: Character moves forward dodging multiple alternating large soft pendulums. One pendulum must realistically hit the character's shoulder and side. Character must perform a genuine falling action on the bridge. Character must not fall into the water. Then must push back up, dodge the last pendulum, and continue. 4. Curved High Wall: Only one wall-run attempt. Must actually run up the wall and successfully grab the top with both hands. 5. Creating Success Expectation: Character is hanging at the top and starts pulling up. Right knee must successfully hook the top. Give the audience the clear expectation she can flip over. 6. Successful Flip: Use arm pull and leg support to bring chest, abdomen, and center of gravity continuously over the edge. Must fully show the process from hanging to flipping. No teleporting, no skipping major exertion steps. 7. Pressing Finish Button: Stand up immediately after flipping over. Step forward and realistically press the red button with right hand. Palm contact and button depression must occur before signal light, buzzer, and timer stop. 8. Victory Face Close-up: Look at camera after success. End with face close-up of gasping, surprise, relief, pride, and real smile as the sole final scene. Full emotional structure: Confident debut → Start challenge → Gradually clumsy → Genuine fall → Persisting → Giving everything to sprint up the wall → Grabbing wall top → Hooking leg for exertion → Successful flip → Pressing button → Victory expression ending. Progresses in real-time throughout. Action speed is natural and real, rhythm is clear, brisk, and sharp. Maintain character consistency, clothing consistency, course continuity, obstacle continuity, real inertia, gravity, collision feedback, and TV live broadcast feel.
